title: Dashboard settings UI and runtime configuration activation (v1.1 Goal A)

findings.area: platform assumption / verification coverage (ADR-021 host ABI)
findings.issue: The activity-log rejection surfacing introduced by task 9.3 depends on the host types MediaBrowser.Model.Activity.IActivityManager and Jellyfin.Database.Implementations.Entities.ActivityLog. The mechanism is verified only against pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 source and unit tests that substitute a DispatchProxy IActivityManager double; no host-guarded or live fact resolves IActivityManager from the pinned host. This is the plugin's only new lower-stability-tier host ABI dependency, and the notifier's write is best-effort (failures are swallowed), so a pinned-host mismatch would silently leave ADR-016 clause 4's administrator surfacing unmet with no signal. Live confirmation is deliberately owned by task 14.3 per the plan, but PLANS.md task 14.3's objective enumerates 'settings page load/save, post-save re-render, cache behavior, and log output/level' without naming the rejected-save activity-log entry that the v1.1 architecture review assigned to it.
evidence: docs/reviews/architecture-review.json (AR-05; documentation_owners task 14.3: 'confirm that a rejected settings-page save writes an administrator-visible Activity log entry and that a valid save does not')
docs/implementation/9.3/reviewer-report.json (finding 9.3-R1: no host-guarded test references IActivityManager; only the recording double)
findings.recommended_action: Make the rejected-save activity-log entry (and the valid-save no-entry case) an explicit line item of the task 14.3 live pinned-host matrix and record the result; optionally add a host-guarded fact that resolves IActivityManager from the pinned host directory. No Phase 9 code change is required, and this does not block the Phase 9 gate because the plan defers live confirmation to 14.3.

findings.area: performance / accepted design interaction with limitation F1
findings.issue: Every successful configuration replacement requests the bounded full-library reconciliation, regardless of whether the changed value is output-affecting. The reconciliation enqueues a work item for every eligible item, and the metadata stage re-reads the provider per work item before the output-fingerprint gate can skip artwork work (limitation F1: no provider inventory cache). A save that only changes, for example, the webhook secret therefore causes a bounded provider-fetch sweep. This is bounded and explicitly accepted by ADR-016 clause 5, but it is non-trivial provider load per save until the Phase 11 inventory cache lands.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Updates/ArtworkPublishingWorkItemProcessor.cs:61-103 (metadata reconciliation runs before the fingerprint gate)
findings.recommended_action: No Phase 9 change (the plan accepts the bounded post-save reconciliation). Ensure Phase 11's inventory cache covers this path, and consider requesting reconciliation only when an output-affecting value changed as a later optimization.

findings.issue: The dashboard page's save handler parses every numeric limit with parseInt(value, 10) and posts the whole configuration. An administrator who clears a numeric field produces NaN, JSON.stringify emits null, and the pinned PluginsController POST deserializes the body into non-nullable int properties, which raises a host deserialization error rather than reaching the plugin's bounded validate/reject path. State is not corrupted (the candidate never reaches persistence) and validation/atomicity/secret handling are unaffected; the impact is an opaque host error instead of the documented bounded rejection.
evidence: src/ArrTags/Plugin.cs:143-157 (validate-before-persist; a deserialization failure never reaches this override)
findings.recommended_action: Optional later hardening: treat an empty numeric input as 'keep the current value', or add a client-side guard, so a cleared field cannot produce a host deserialization error. Not required for the Phase 9 gate.

findings.issue: Two LOW findings from the task 9.1 test-quality review remain open: 9.1-TQ1 (the host-guarded fact pins the pinned PluginsController's private _serializerOptions field and the POST route template but never asserts that the POST action actually uses that field, so a future host that kept the field but changed the action would still pass) and 9.1-TQ5 (a process-global AssemblyLoadContext.Default.Resolving handler in a static Lazy is never unregistered). Both are non-blocking: the unguarded round-trip tests are the actual non-vacuous proof of the collection fix, and the pattern is shared with pre-existing host-guarded tests.
findings.recommended_action: Track for the release/documentation pass; optional strengthening (invoke the real POST action, or unregister the ALC resolver in a disposable fixture).

findings.area: documentation precision / ADR-016 clause-5 implementation note
findings.issue: The ADR-016 implementation note (and the matching limitations F2 / architecture section 6 / data-model 3.12 wording) enumerates the construction-captured limits as 'the artifact-size/decode limits and the StateRepository-backed render work-cache TTL/quota and terminal-provenance retention values'. ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes is also construction-captured (SourceArtifactStore reads repository.Limits.ArtifactStorageQuotaBytes at construction). The note's 'some singletons capture ...' phrasing is illustrative and clause 5 is correctly not rewritten, so this is a precision nit rather than an overclaim.
findings.recommended_action: Optionally add 'and the artifact/provenance storage quota' or state explicitly that the enumeration is illustrative. No action required.

findings.issue: docs/implementation/9.3/reviewer-report.json is byte-identical to reviewer-report.attempt-2.json (the first reviewer attempt, which approved), while the final APPROVED review is reviewer-report.attempt-4.json.
